text:
MARKING SCHEME
GRADE 10: HRE
SECTION A: [30 MARKS]
1. (a) Identification: Matsya (The Fish Avatar). (1 mk)
 (b) Comparison: (4 mks)
 Matsya: Streamlined body, scales, and fins adapted for aquatic movement and breathing through gills.
 Varah: Robust mammalian structure, tusks for digging, adapted for terrestrial/muddy environments and
 lung breathing.
 (c) True/False: True. (1 mk)
 (d) Explanation: Buddhahood emphasizes the "Nine Qualities" including compassion and equanimity. In a
 school like those in Kilifi, this promotes tolerance of different ethnic/religious backgrounds and reduces
 bullying or social friction. (4 mks)
2. (a) Name: X – Tabla; Y – Harmonium. (2 mks)
 (b) Matching: (4 mks)
 I — B (Wood and Animal Skin)
 II — C (Gourd and Metal Strings)
 III — A (Wood and Reeds)
 IV — D (Wood and stretched hide)
 (c) Function: It provides a continuous harmonic drone (the root note) which acts as a reference point for the
 vocalist to maintain pitch. (2 mks)
 (d) Mention: Isukuti and Dudu dance (or any relevant local dance using percussion). (2 mks)
3. (a) Definition: The universal law of cause and effect where every action (physical or mental) has a corresponding
 consequence. (2 mks)
 (b) Distinction:
 Sukrit: Actions aligned with Hukam (God's will), leading to spiritual growth and "Sarbat da Bhala" (well-
 being of all). (2 mks)
 Dukrit: Actions driven by ego or vice that contradict spiritual laws. (2 mks)
 (c) Outline: (4 mks)
 Prakriti: Nature of the karma.
 Sthiti: Duration the karma stays with the soul.
 Anubhag: Intensity of the fruit/result.
 Pradesh: Quantity of karmic particles attached.
4. (a) Identification: Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. (1 mk)
 (b) List: Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka. (3 mks)
 (c) Description: They are "Shruti" (that which is heard), revealed to ancient Rishis (sages) during deep
 meditation; they were not "authored" by humans but "received." (3 mks)
 (d) Explanation: It presents "Dharma-Sankat" (ethical dilemmas). By studying characters like Yudhishthira or
 Arjuna, learners learn to prioritize duty over personal gain and the importance of righteousness in leadership.
 (4 mks)
 (e) Name: Tulsidas. (1 mk)
 (f) Challenges: Oral transmission risks (memorization errors), destruction of physical manuscripts during
 invasions, and difficulties in translating ancient Sanskrit/Pali/Gurmukhi into modern languages. (3 mks)
5. (a) Identification: Dudu dance (1 mk)
 (b) Examination: As the frequency (tempo/BPM) of the drum (Dhol) increases, the kinetic energy and pace of
 the Bhangra dancers increase proportionally to maintain synchronization with the rhythm. (4 mks)
 (c) Name: Dandiya (sticks) or Dhol. (2 mks)
 (d) Categorization: (4 mks)
 I. Secular-Patriotic
 II. Sacred/Religious
 III. Folk
 IV. Secular-Patriotic
 (e) Explanation: Scientifically, correct pronunciation creates specific sound vibrations (Shabad) that affect the
 nervous system; spiritually, it ensures the original divine message of the Gurus is preserved without distortion.
 (4 mks)
6. (a) Principle: Ahimsa (Non-violence). Defined as the total avoidance of harming any living being through
 thought, word, or deed. (3 mks)
 (b) List: Rishabhdeva, Parshavnath, Neminath, Mallinath, and Bhagwan Mahavir. (5 mks)
 (c) Contribution: He is credited with teaching humans the "Asi, Masi, and Krishi" (Arts of defense, writing,
 and agriculture), transitioning society from migratory to sedentary farming. (3 mks)
 (d) Discussion: It advocates for "Non-possessiveness." If Kenyans take only what is needed (sustainability)
 rather than accumulating excess, it reduces the strain on natural forests, water bodies, and wildlife, ensuring
 resources for future generations. (5 mks)
 (e) Qualities: Examples include: Supatipanno (Good conduct), Ujupatipanno (Upright conduct), Wisdom
 (Panna), Compassion (Metta), etc. (Accept any 4 valid qualities). (4 mks)
